name: Genshin Impact mobile HUD (default layout)
notes: Calibrated on a 2400x1080 Android emulator (default touch layout, zh-CN client). x/y are control centres on the reference screen; the anchor edge keeps its distance when the aspect ratio differs. w/h are tap-area sizes. Probes are reference-space pixels with expected RGB; the first screen whose probes all match is reported. Recalibrate with `pnpm agent layout --layout layouts/genshin-impact.json --out artifacts/layout.png`. Interaction prompt lists (1–5 entries, centred at y 538 with a 90 px pitch) were measured with 1 and 3 entries and extrapolated for 2, 4 and 5; reply options were measured with two options only. Button `text` and screen `texts` boxes are OCR regions: prompt labels span x 1480–1760, reply options x 1535–1800, and the dialogue speaker and two subtitle lines sit above the bottom edge.
playbook: These are habits of an experienced Genshin Impact player. They are advice, not rules: you choose every step, and when the screen shows something they do not cover, decide as a careful player would.
Quest first: the tracked quest is the main thread. Side activities (exploring, picking things up, fighting) are worth a short detour only when they are right in front of you or in the way.

When code reads the tracked quest as far away, a player teleports near it with Teleport near quest 传送到任务附近 instead of running there; when code reads it as close, the player walks with Go to quest marker 前往任务标记 and keeps walking while the distance keeps shrinking.

When code reads no quest distance on the HUD, or code found no tracked quest on the world map at the last teleport, a player tracks the quest again with Track quest 追踪任务 before teleporting or walking; opening the map again finds nothing.
When Track quest 追踪任务 reports the quest is far and leaves the world map open on it, a player teleports right away from that map.

When code measured that walking made no progress once, a player looks at what is in the way before walking again: around a cliff face, rock or building they go around the side that looks open (Go around left 向左绕行 or Go around right 向右绕行); a low wall or slope they just walk over again (climbing is fine when the quest is above); water or a deep drop they avoid by going around or teleporting. When it made no progress twice or more in a row, the player stops walking into the obstacle and teleports to a nearby teleport point, then walks again from there.

When a screenshot of the screen is given, a player uses it like their own eyes: what is ahead of the character, whether the path is open, whether enemies, NPCs or chests are in view. Code's text facts (distances, health, screen names) are measured and stay authoritative where they say something.

While swimming, a player teleports rather than swimming on: swimming drains stamina and the shore may be a cliff. While climbing, the player lets the walk finish the climb when the quest is above (高处).

When the walk to the quest reports arrived with the area changed, the player looks at what appeared (a prompt, an NPC, an enemy) and deals with it. When it reports searched (nothing happened inside the quest area), the player does not walk into the same area again; they explore nearby, pick up or talk to whatever prompt appears, or look for enemies to fight.

Interaction prompts on the right are what a player presses next: pick up items, open chests, talk to NPCs, especially when the prompt or NPC name matches the quest. With several prompts, the one matching the quest objective comes first. A 坐下 (sit down) prompt is just a chair or stool, never the quest: a player ignores it and keeps going toward the quest.
In a conversation, a player continues it; at reply options they pick the reply that moves the quest forward, and avoid replies that only end the chat or ask about unrelated things.
When an enemy is visible or indicated, a player approaches it, and fights once it is near. A fight that just ended clear is followed by going back to the quest.

When code reads the active character's health as low and no enemy is attacking, a player heals at a Statue of The Seven with Heal at Statue 七天神像回血 before going on. A player also heals there when the last fight left teammates downed with no food to revive them. When code says healing failed from here, the player does not try it again on the spot: they go on with the quest carefully (avoiding fights), or teleport somewhere else first and heal from there.
A map, menu or quest log that is still open after a routine finished is closed with BACK before playing on in the open world.

A player does not repeat the same action three times in a row when it keeps giving the same result: they switch to a different approach (teleport instead of walking, track the quest again, explore around, or fight).

routines.label: Go to quest marker 前往任务标记
routines.description: Code turns the camera toward the tracked quest's yellow marker on the minimap and runs toward it for about 25 seconds, longer for a far quest (about 1 second per 1.7m of quest distance, up to 3 minutes; it keeps going for another 30 seconds each time the quest distance has shrunk by 10m, up to 6 minutes; longer again when screenshots are slow), re-aiming as it goes. It walks in a straight line, which suits open country outside towns; in a town or other built-up place (streets, houses, roofs and walls close together on the screenshot or minimap), use Find a way to quest 沿路前往任务 instead. Every few seconds it double-jumps, so running off a cliff opens the wind glider 风之翼 instead of falling; while gliding it keeps steering toward the marker without jumping. It stops when the marker reaches the character (arrived), when someone to talk to appears, when the screen leaves the open world, or when the character is stuck. The quest distance text shows the remaining distance; use it again while the distance keeps shrinking. If the quest is more than 150m away, use teleport first instead of walking; walking that far can lead into water or cliffs. When the quest marks an area (a yellow ring on the minimap, HUD 已到达任务区域), it walks into the ring, then stands still a few seconds in case the quest reacts; with no change it walks circles inside the ring for about 20 seconds. It reports arrived with area changed as soon as something happens there (a new screen such as a talk or pickup prompt, or the ring going away), or searched when nothing happened; then look at the screen or try something else (explore, interact, fight) rather than walking into the area again. It stops with attacked when code measures the active character losing health on the way (enemies are hitting it, maybe out of view); then fight with Fight 战斗.

routines.label: Explore 随机游走
routines.description: Code walks the character a short distance roughly straight ahead (where the camera faces, within 30° either side): up to 5 short hops of about one step each, checking the screen standing still after every hop, and stops as soon as a new interaction prompt appears, a new enemy HP bar appears (enemy), the screen leaves the open world, or the character stays stuck. Use it to look for something to pick up, talk to or interact with; if nothing appears, use it again to keep exploring further. It stops with attacked when code measures the active character losing health; then fight with Fight 战斗.

routines.label: Continue dialogue 自动推进对话
routines.description: Code taps through the conversation until reply options appear (then you choose one), the open world returns (the conversation ended), or it stops changing. Up to 60 seconds.

routines.label: Fight 战斗
routines.description: Code fights nearby enemies: each active character uses elemental skill, a few normal attacks, then tries the burst, then the next teammate who is still standing is switched in (a downed teammate is tapped once to open the revive dialog and revived with the preselected food; when no food is left the dialog is closed with 取消 and the result reports noFood, so heal at a Statue of The Seven to revive them). It always fights one round first (attacks turn towards the nearest enemy), then watches for red enemy HP bars: if none appeared it stops (no_enemy), and once they have been gone for 2 checks in a row it stops (clear). It does not walk towards enemies, so get close first; otherwise it runs up to 45 seconds. While code measures the active character still losing health it keeps fighting even without visible bars.

routines.label: Approach enemy 接近敌人
routines.description: Code looks for the nearest enemy: an HP bar, or a distant enemy's level label (Lv.) when it is too far away for a bar. If none is in view it first turns towards a red off-screen enemy arrow and walks a step towards it, and otherwise turns the camera around in place (a full circle, ending facing the same way as before). It then walks towards the enemy, turning the camera to keep it centred, and stops once the enemy is within fighting range (near), when no enemy is found all around (no_enemy), when it loses sight of the enemy (lost), or when the character is stuck. Use it whenever an enemy is visible or indicated, even far away, and to search for enemies before exploring further; use Fight 战斗 after it reports the enemy is near. It stops with attacked when code measures the active character losing health before reaching a bar (an enemy is already hitting it, maybe out of view); then fight with Fight 战斗 where you stand.

routines.label: Go around left 向左绕行
routines.description: Only offered when the last walk to the quest made no progress. Code first walks to the left of the current camera direction for about 3 seconds, then walks to the quest marker like Go to quest marker 前往任务标记. Choose it when the screenshot shows the way ahead blocked (a cliff, wall, water, rocks or a building) and the left side looks open.

routines.label: Go around right 向右绕行
routines.description: Only offered when the last walk to the quest made no progress. Code first walks to the right of the current camera direction for about 3 seconds, then walks to the quest marker like Go to quest marker 前往任务标记. Choose it when the screenshot shows the way ahead blocked (a cliff, wall, water, rocks or a building) and the right side looks open.

routines.label: Find a way to quest 沿路前往任务
routines.description: Code reads the minimap as open ground (streets, paths, grass) and obstacles (roofs, walls, water), plans a way around the obstacles toward the quest marker, and keeps steering along it without turning the camera. This is the way to walk in towns: choose it when the screenshot or minimap shows the character in a town or other built-up place (streets, houses, roofs and walls close together). Outside towns, use Go to quest marker 前往任务标记, which walks straight. Code also switches to it by itself when straight walks to the quest made no progress twice in a row. It cannot plan climbs or height changes, and its reading of 璃月 roofs is unreliable.

routines.label: Teleport near quest 传送到任务附近
routines.description: Code tracks the quest again in the quest log (停止追踪, then 追踪) so the game opens the world map centred on it, zooms the map in fully, picks the unlocked teleport waypoint or Statue of The Seven nearest to the quest (zooming out step by step when none is near), confirms its teleport panel by OCR, taps 传送 once and waits for the open world to load. Use it when the tracked quest distance is more than 150m instead of walking; if code finds the quest close to you on the map it closes the map without teleporting, and you should walk there with navigate. While swimming it teleports even to a close quest, because swimming toward it can end at a cliff. On failure the world map may stay open; press BACK to close it.

routines.label: Heal at Statue 七天神像回血
routines.description: Code opens the world map and teleports to a visible unlocked Statue of The Seven so its automatic blessing can restore a low-health party. Use it when the active character has at most 25% health. If no statue is visible, it zooms the map out up to three steps; if still none, it leaves the map open and continuous play falls back to another activity.

routines.label: Track quest 追踪任务
routines.description: Code makes sure a quest is tracked. If the HUD already shows a quest distance it does nothing, unless teleport just found no quest on the map (the quest is in another region): then it re-tracks it anyway. Otherwise it opens the quest log 任务 and taps 追踪目标 for the selected quest (usually the newest); a quest that is tracked but shows no HUD distance (it is in another region) is untracked and tracked again. A near quest returns to the open world and the HUD shows it (tracked). A far quest makes the game open the world map on it; code leaves that map open (tracked_far) so you can teleport there right away. Use it when no tracked quest objective or distance is shown on the HUD, or after teleport found no quest on the map.
